name: GTA 6
description: GTA 6'nın suç dünyasına uygun çeviri: sokak ağzı, argo ve küfür korunur. Karakter, mekân, silah ve marka adları çevrilmez.
world: Set in Leonida, a satirical Florida: neon Vice City (Miami parody), swamps, beach towns and the Keys. Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, a modern Bonnie and Clyde, are lovers and partners in crime caught up in heists, drug deals, gangs and cops. Satire of money, guns and viral social media. People talk street: slang, threats, dark jokes, heavy swearing.
rules: Sound like a good Turkish crime-movie dub: natural street talk, informal "sen" (formal speakers stay formal). Never translate word for word.
Translate slang and idioms by meaning, not literally: we're cooked = yandık, he's toast = onun işi bitti, my bad = benim hatam.
In a shootout, "I'm out" means out of ammo.
Keep swearing as strong as the source (fuck ≈ siktir, shit ≈ hassiktir/kahretsin, filler "fucking" ≈ lan), never adding any that isn't there.
Never translate slurs about ethnicity, religion or sexual orientation: use a plain insult or drop it. Between friends, the n-word becomes "kanka" or nothing.
Never translate names of people, places, gangs, shops, brands, weapons or vehicles; add Turkish suffixes with an apostrophe: Lucia'yı, Vice City'de.
Guns or cars called "baby"/"babies" are the item itself: say "bu güzellik" or "bunlar", never "bebek".
Button prompts: keep button names exactly as written (L2, R2, X, Square) and write short Turkish commands.
If dialogue and a button prompt got mixed in one line, untangle them and translate both, dialogue first.
Translate Spanish words too (pendejo = gerizekalı, mija = kızım), except well-known ones like amigo.
